newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - July 28.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Monday:
* New York's ailing hospitals are to be offered $1.25 billion in federal aid over five years to reinvent themselves for the age of managed care.
* The record industry has decided to introduce a new format to replace the compact disk.
* Last week Russian President Boris Yeltsin signed a series of decrees that will introduce the most fundamental military reforms in the country's modern history.
* Gov. William Weld of Massachusetts plans to retire plans to resign today to devote full attention to his embattled nomination for the post of Ambassador to Mexico.
* Mott Haven in New York's Bronx was once home to Irish immigrants but is now attracting Mexicans, who are at the bottom of the ladder in community influence and earning power.

* While running has become a casual exercise for many Americans, others indulge in ultramarathons ranging from 50 to 100 miles as a method of achieving self fulfillment through the breakdown of personal limitations.
